title: Handle 'time saved is not P&L'
clearance: Rewritten draft; pending SME and partner clearance

blocks.x: Value objections are a test of credibility. Answer them with evidence and transparency, and don't get defensive or lean on salesmanship.

Glean's Value Playbook prepares teams for the most frequent CFO and CIO challenges, such as "Where did the saved time go?" and "These are just benchmarks." It also asks teams to always identify which assumptions are benchmark-based and which are customer-specific.

blocks.caption: Responding to value objections
head: You hear
Respond with
rows: Agreement, the labeled assumptions, and the validation plan
The recapture and reallocation assumptions, and their owner
Which inputs are customer-specific, and how benchmark inputs will be replaced with measured data
Corroboration from telemetry and system-of-record data

items: **Ask** what evidence would change their view.
**Show** the assumptions, the range, and the current evidence level.
**Agree** on a test, with an owner and a date.

blocks.label: Boundary
blocks.x: Don't defend an inflated number. Revise it in front of them if they're right.
Give the champion a story they can carry

Glean's value-selling training is a reminder of why objection handling matters: assume Glean is not a budgeted initiative. When a finance leader challenges your numbers, the champion will have to answer the same challenge later, without you. Handle the objection so the champion leaves with an answer they can repeat.

blocks.title: Handling an evidence or value objection
blocks.alt: A four-step pattern for handling objections: acknowledge the concern, ask what evidence would resolve it, show the source and assumptions, and agree how it will be checked.

items.label: Agree
items.detail: How and when it will be checked
